create.title: Frequency-first divisor bound for the terminal M1 block
create.statement_tex: Let B_1(D,L;X)=sum_h u_(L,H)(h) sum_(d in D_D) chi_4(d)w_D(d)e(hX/d), where D_D lies in a fixed shell d asymp D, possibly with the hard truncation d<=floor(sqrt X), |w_D|<<1, and ||u||_infty+sum|Delta u|<<1/L. Uniformly for real X>=2 and 1<=L<=D<=X^(1/2), B_1(D,L;X)<<_epsilon X^epsilon(1+D/L). Therefore for the actual Vaaler block with H_D asymp D X^(-1/4), every terminal shell L asymp H_D is O_epsilon(X^(1/4+epsilon)) throughout X^(1/4)<=D<=X^(1/2), including the hard endpoint. At D asymp X^(1/2), the accepted top M1 transform then gives the normalized signed-cone estimate on the terminal h-shell only.
create.next_action: Remove the terminal M1 line from every case split. Do not extrapolate the D/L estimate to lower frequency shells.

create.title: Tao--Trudgian--Yang exponent-pair wedge for M1
create.statement_tex: Let D=X^delta and L=X^ell in the active M1 triangle, with the actual fixed discrete-BV denominator profile and Vaaler coefficient. Resolve chi_4(d) into d=1,3 mod 4 and apply the Tao--Trudgian--Yang pair (89/1282,997/1282) to the resulting shifted reciprocal model phases. Then B_1(D,L;X)<<_epsilon X^([89(1+ell)+819delta]/1282+epsilon), so the X^(1/4+epsilon) target holds when 178ell+1638delta<=463. The theorem is pointwise in real X and includes the hard top BV profile; it does not apply to arbitrary denominator coefficients.
create.next_action: Use the wedge only for the accepted fixed-BV dyadic profiles. Preserve the residual corridor outside it.

create.title: Exact Round-10 M1 frequency coverage and residual corridor
create.statement_tex: In Omega={(delta,ell):1/4<=delta<=1/2, 0<=ell<=delta-1/4}, the M1 frequency-first divisor bound covers the terminal line ell=delta-1/4, the full second-derivative estimate covers (1/2,0), and the M1 TTY pair covers 178ell+1638delta<=463. Naive chi_4 Abel adds no active target region. Relative to these proved direct estimates, the exact remaining set is U_1={(delta,ell) in Omega: 0<=ell<delta-1/4 and 178ell+1638delta>463} minus {(1/2,0)}. All bounds use the actual Vaaler coefficient and accepted fixed-BV spatial profiles, including the hard top profile.
create.next_action: Attack only U_1. Retain the character-divisor coefficient in the frequency-first near-product window or use an equivalent signed product-phase estimate.

update.next_action: Attack the exact residual corridor U_1 through the signed short-interval character-divisor coefficient retained by the frequency-first near-product expansion. The terminal line, certified TTY wedge, and point (1/2,0) are solved.
The terminal h-shell is proved by the direct divisor estimate. Prove only the middle/lower hard-top shells, equivalently the intersection of this cone with U_1.

reject.reason: Abel summation against bounded partial sums costs total phase variation hX/D across a length-D shell, not the one-step derivative hX/D^2; after the h-block this adds no active target region.
The first-derivative model-phase hypothesis must be checked. The safe M1 transfer resolves chi_4 into residue classes and applies the reciprocal theorem after d=4n+r.
The cited monomial estimates require independent two- or three-variable separable phases and do not directly apply to the one-variable character-twisted reciprocal block.
Bettin--Chandee treats modular inverses in Kloosterman fractions with essential coprimality and norm hypotheses, not the real reciprocal phase X/d.
